LEGAL NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK

=== STRATEGIC OVERVIEW ===
Objective: Secure favorable commercial terms while protecting IP assets and limiting liability exposure. Approach: Collaborative but firm; lead with value creation, defend deal breakers absolutely, deploy fallbacks sequentially.

=== SEQUENCING GUIDANCE ===
Phase 1 - Commercial Framework (Days 1-3): Pricing, volume discounts, payment terms. Establish economic baseline before discussing risk allocation.
Phase 2 - Operational Terms (Days 4-6): Delivery timelines, performance standards, termination for convenience (90-day notice).
Phase 3 - Risk Allocation (Days 7-9): Liability caps, indemnification scope, IP licensing vs. ownership.
Phase 4 - Exit Protections (Days 10-12): Auto-renewal prevention, assignment restrictions, non-compete boundaries.

=== PRIORITY PLAYBOOKS ===

PRIORITY 1: Competitive Pricing with Volume Discounts
Talk Track: "We anticipate significant scale in this relationship. To align incentives, we need a tiered pricing structure that rewards volume commitment with meaningful discounts—specifically [X]% at [Y] units and [Z]% at [A] units. This ensures mutual growth."
Tactics: Anchor high on discount expectations. Reference market benchmarks. Bundle with longer commitment periods if needed.
Fallback: Accept market-standard pricing with annual rate adjustment caps not exceeding CPI+2% or 5%, whichever is lower.

PRIORITY 2: Clear Delivery Timelines with Enforceable Penalties
Talk Track: "Operational reliability is critical to our business planning. We require specific delivery milestones with liquidated damages of [X]% per week of delay, capped at [Y]% of order value. This isn't punitive—it's risk allocation for missed commitments."
Tactics: Define "delay" precisely (business days vs. calendar days). Exclude force majeure and customer-caused delays.
Fallback: Allow reasonable delay notifications (48-72 hours advance notice) in lieu of monetary penalties for first occurrence, provided recovery plan is submitted.

PRIORITY 3: Limit Liability to Direct Damages Only
Talk Track: "We operate in a high-risk environment where consequential damages could theoretically exceed company value. We must cap liability to direct, proven damages and explicitly exclude consequential, incidental, and lost profits. This is standard for our industry."
Tactics: Define "direct damages" as costs to cure or replace. Carve out confidentiality breaches and IP indemnification from the cap.
Fallback: Accept aggregate liability cap limited to 12 months of fees paid under the agreement, with specific carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnification.

PRIORITY 4: Broad Intellectual Property Licensing Rights
Talk Track: "We need comprehensive usage rights to integrate your solution into our operations. We require a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use, modify, and create derivative works for internal business purposes, with right to sublicense to affiliates."
Tactics: Distinguish between ownership (deal breaker) and license (negotiable). Limit sublicense rights to affiliates only, not third parties.
Fallback: Accept restricted license limited to specific named use cases (e.g., "internal data processing and analytics only") with no modification rights, terminable upon agreement expiration.

PRIORITY 5: Termination for Convenience with 90-Day Notice
Talk Track: "Business needs evolve. We require flexibility to terminate without cause upon 90 days advance written notice, allowing orderly transition. This doesn't reflect lack of commitment—it reflects prudent business planning."
Tactics: Negotiate transition assistance period post-termination. Ensure data return/destruction obligations are mutual.
Fallback: Accept termination for cause only with 30-day cure period, provided "cause" is narrowly defined (material breach, insolvency, violation of law).

=== DEAL BREAKER DEFENSE PROTOCOLS ===

DEAL BREAKER 1: Unlimited Liability or Broad Indemnification for Third-Party Claims
Defense: "We cannot accept uncapped exposure for third-party claims. Our hard line is: (a) indemnification limited to third-party IP infringement claims only, (b) liability capped at fees paid, and (c) no indemnification for our own negligence or misuse. If unlimited liability remains on the table, we walk."

DEAL BREAKER 2: Automatic Renewal Clauses Without Prior Written Consent
Defense: "Auto-renewal creates budgetary and operational risk. We require affirmative written consent 60 days prior to renewal, or the agreement terminates. No evergreen clauses. If auto-renewal is mandatory, we need termination rights exercisable up to 30 days prior to renewal date."

DEAL BREAKER 3: Assignment or Transfer of Intellectual Property Ownership
Defense: "We will not transfer ownership of our pre-existing IP or jointly developed improvements. License rights only—non-exclusive, revocable upon termination. Any language suggesting 'work for hire,' 'assignment,' or 'transfer of ownership' is unacceptable. We license; we do not sell our IP."

DEAL BREAKER 4: Non-Compete or Exclusivity Restrictions Limiting Future Operations
Defense: "We operate in multiple verticals. We cannot accept exclusivity or non-compete restrictions broader than the specific scope of this agreement. No restrictions on: (a) serving other customers in same industry, (b) developing similar technologies independently, (c) operating in geographic territories. If exclusivity is required, limit to 12 months and specific named accounts only."

DEAL BREAKER 5: Payment Terms Exceeding Net 60 Days Without Applicable Interest Charges
Defense: "Our cash flow requirements mandate payment within net 30, maximum net 60. Beyond net 60, we require interest at 1.5% per month (18% annual) or maximum allowable by law. No payment terms contingent on customer acceptance, testing, or milestone completion unless clearly defined and time-limited. If extended payment terms are required, we need adequate security or letter of credit."

=== TACTICAL GUIDANCE ===

Opening Gambit: Lead with Priority 1 (Pricing) to establish economic baseline, then immediately move to Priority 5 (Termination) to signal you have options.

Concession Strategy: Never give away fallbacks for free. Trade fallback acceptance for movement on deal breakers. Example: "We can accept the 12-month liability cap if you remove the auto-renewal clause."

Silence Points: After stating deal breakers, stop talking. First party to speak loses leverage.

Documentation: All verbal agreements must be confirmed via email before end of business day. No "we'll clean it up in the drafting" concessions.

Walk-Away Preparation: Identify alternative suppliers before entering Phase 3. Be prepared to suspend negotiations for 48 hours if deal breakers are pressed.

=== CLOSING CHECKLIST ===
□ Liability capped at 12 months fees or lower
□ Auto-renewal removed or converted to affirmative consent
□ IP ownership retained; license rights only granted
□ No broad non-compete or exclusivity
□ Payment terms ≤net 60 or interest charged
□ Termination for convenience (90-day) or narrow cause (30-day cure)
□ Delivery penalties defined or notification system agreed
□ Pricing with volume discounts or rate caps
□ Broad IP license or restricted use case license secured
